_comment: The guided-install contract of the PIM Manager (GUIDED-INSTALL 4.1-4.6). Invardia's wizard asks exactly these questions and writes the answers to config.json for tools/setup/Install-PimManager.ps1, which validates them again (Test-PimInstallConfig). 'maps' = what the answer drives. Kept in step with Install-PimManager by tests/Test-PimGuidedInstall.ps1.
licenceOrKey: -LicencePath is required unless config.json carries enrollmentKey: an enrollment key (framework 8.6) makes the install claim the tenant at Invardia, which returns the licence and the install key.

exitCodes.1: a step failed -- fix it and -Resume
exitCodes.3: bad answers or a bad licence -- nothing was changed

parameters.help: The Microsoft Entra tenant PIM manages. The licence is bound to it.
The Azure subscription that hosts PIM (Container Apps, Azure SQL).
Some subscriptions cannot create new Azure SQL servers in West Europe -- the installer checks the region first.
Created when it does not exist; an existing one is reused.
Set from the licence in the bundle, not asked.
The guided install builds the external shape: the PIM Manager is reachable on the internet behind Microsoft Entra sign-in. A private-network install is a consultant-led setup.
A /23 or larger (Azure Container Apps), inside the VNet range.

single = this tenant only. managed = a tenant managed by an MSP (managing company): needs the enrollment key that company got from Invardia; the install links it to the managing tenant. A managing tenant is set up with support.
parameters.maps: single: Scenario S2 + the licence; managed: Invoke-PimMspBuild -Role Slave (S6) -EnrollmentKey

parameters.help: Optional for single, required for managed. The Invardia enrollment key (ek-...). With it no licence file is needed: the install claims this tenant at Invardia, which returns the licence and the install key. A bearer secret: never shown, never logged, removed from config.json once the licence is registered.
parameters.maps: the enroll step (claim) + the licence step

parameters.help: Managed tenant only, optional: the name prefix(es) of the admin accounts the managing company manages in this tenant (e.g. Admin-). Used only to report a naming mismatch; leave it empty and set the admin account patterns in Settings later.
Managed tenant only: the ring of this tenant for the managing company's policy bundle (2 = production).
Who may sign in to the PIM Manager. Default: the super-admins.
Every member account of the tenant may sign in (guests never).

Optional. Also give the PIM engine User Access Administrator at the tenant root management group, so it can assign the Azure resource roles you delegate. Off by default: the engine always gets read-only Reader there (Discovery), and Get Started shows the command to add User Access Administrator later.
Default: you (the account running the install).

The mailbox PIM sends from. Created by the install when the installer holds an ACTIVE Exchange Administrator or Global Administrator role (both sending identities get the scoped send right); without one the install completes and the end-of-install check shows the Get Started > Mail sender command.
Who gets the alerts (engine failures, drift, break-glass use, ...). Default: the super-admins' mailboxes. A list that is already set is never overwritten.
The Invardia Support app of this tenant (pre-filled from the support environment). Empty = no support access.
troubleshoot = read the database and its schema; setup = also repair and upgrade (SQL admin group member, owner of PIM's own apps and groups).

steps.title: Azure SQL in the chosen region

minimalConfig.claimedByInvardiaNeeds: -LicencePath <the claimed licence file>. ONE claimant per install: with installKey in the answers Install-PimManager never claims (an enrollmentKey beside it is ignored, never sent). managing = the claim's managing block { bundleStorage, container, signingKeyIds[], tenantId? }.
minimalConfig.managing: a managing tenant (MSP) is not a guided install: Invoke-PimMspBuild -Role Master with support

requiredRights: Owner, or Contributor + User Access Administrator, on the subscription (required -- the preflight stops without it)
Privileged Role Administrator, active (recommended) -- without it the SQL admin group, the Graph permissions and the sign-in consent end as hand-off actions with the exact command
Exchange Administrator or Global Administrator, active, for the notification mailbox (optional -- without it the end-of-install check ends with the Get Started > Mail sender follow-up)

Owner or User Access Administrator at the tenant root management group (recommended; a Global Administrator who turned on Access management for Azure resources) -- the install gives the engine Reader there; without that right the end-of-install check ends with a WARNING and the exact command for that person (the install is not stopped -- owner decision of 2026-10-08)
runsIn: Azure Cloud Shell (PowerShell 7) as the signed-in account -- never a secret. Also PowerShell 7 or Windows PowerShell 5.1 on Windows with the Azure CLI.
licence: A Pro licence bound to the tenant above (a trial or a paid licence). A licence for another tenant, or one that names no tenant, is refused (exit 3).
costStatement: About 27 USD a month (Azure Container Apps scale to zero, Basic registry, Azure SQL serverless-sized, external).
